events.title: Manchester Baby runs first stored program
events.summary: The Manchester Small-Scale Experimental Machine ran its first program on June 21, 1948 — the first program executed on an electronic [stored-program] computer.
events.about: Frederic Williams, Tom Kilburn, and Geoff Toothill built the Baby to test Williams tubes — a cathode-ray-tube memory. Kilburn's 17-instruction program proved instructions and data could live in the same electronic store, the model every computer uses today.

narrative.whyChosen: The Baby was the first machine to run a program stored in electronic memory.
narrative.whyImportant: It validated [stored-program] architecture before EDSAC and commercial computers.
narrative.problemSolved: Researchers needed proof that electronic memory could hold both code and data for rewritable programs.
